mechanics.definition: A condition where the PC rolling the dice also rolls an additional 1d6. This can be assigned in many ways.

Similar to Advantage, this term applies to dice rolls; this condition means that the PC rolling uses a 1d10 and a 1d6 instead of a 1d20. This effectively downgrades your point count total from a possible 20 to a 16.
The roll to try to beat the difficulty level assigned to a task by the Arbiter based on their chart. They consider your skills, abilities, and the current situation when assigning a difficulty level.

A 1d6 roll used as a 50/50 chance roll. Even is always the best or positive outcome; odd is always the worst or negative. The Arbiter can assign these as a chance roll for odd requests or can be applied by items or rules. A coin may be used for this purpose as well.
When you roll a maximum dice amount on your damage roll (not your attack roll). This is not a critical hit. Tartaria Prima does not have a crit.

A game mechanic representing where a faction holds you, earned by completing their contracts, hunts and mysteries, by gifts, by returning their sigils, and by trade. It is never exchanged or spent — it is a threshold you stand above, and it stays where you left it. High enough and their gear, their restricted holdings and their deeper work open to you; 20 lets you join. Low enough and it turns: below zero their patrols will engage you, and at −25 they hunt you on their own ground. Tracked in-game as faction standing.

Affected players and NPCs cannot see for 2 turns and cannot complete any tasks needing eyesight. At the beginning of the third turn, they roll a 1d6 for an even/odd roll. If odd, they roll for a disadvantage for one turn, then return to normal. If they roll even, they return to normal on that turn.
When caused, ignites whatever item it is used on; it is engulfed in flames and continues to burn until extinguished. Ignite causes burn damage to start.

lore_terms.definition: The Aether-infused undead of Tartaria, buried by the Great Mud Flood and trapped in an ethereal plane of peace. When the Aetherstone mud encasing them is disturbed, they reawaken with powerful Aetheric abilities, emerging hostile to all intruders who threaten their longed-for rest.
The hardened, impenetrable form of mud that encased Tartarian cities after the Mud Flood. Aetherstone is extremely durable and resistant to excavation due to its Aetheric properties.

Guardians formed from Aether-infused mud surrounding a Tartarian citizen unable to make it to safety during the flood, believed to protect Tartarian ruins and artifacts. Their ability to blend with the mud makes them nearly invisible until provoked.

The unique Tartarian practice of blending engineering with Aetheric principles to create structures that channel Aetheric Power. Examples include self-repairing buildings and defenses that create illusions or repel intruders.

Disturbances caused by residual Aetheric energy in the Mud Seas and other Tartarian ruins, leading to magnetic field fluctuations, disorienting time effects, and phenomena like aetheric lightning and hallucinations.
Powerful automatons of varying sizes that protect Tartarian locations. These machines, from drones to towering war constructs, were programmed to defend important sites with lethal precision.
Locations with dense Aetheric energy from Tartarian structures, where time and space distort. Many Aetheric Ruins contain valuable relics, ghostly apparitions, and unpredictable energy phenomena.
A massive construct designed to protect Tartarian sites from intruders, considered a final challenge for those who attempt to activate or deactivate key Tartarian systems.
A Tartarian spell used to repair, manipulate, or redirect Aetheric relics. Users of this spell need a high Arcana skill to control or restore ancient Tartarian devices safely.

The catastrophic event that buried Tartaria in Aether-charged mud, encasing cities and technology beneath impenetrable Aetherstone. Triggered by a malfunction in Aetheric Power experiments, it led to Tartaria's fall and the rise of factions trying to control its legacy.
Aetheric constructs made from mud, created either by Mud Magic or failed Mud Tech experiments. These beings are immensely strong but unpredictable, sometimes turning on their creators.

A primitive form of energy manipulation practiced by those in contact with Aetheric-charged mud, used to control terrain, heal, or create Mud Golems. It carries physical and mental risks for practitioners.
A crude adaptation of Aetheric technology derived from the resources found in Aetheric-charged mud. Its use is dangerous, with unstable properties that often backfire or malfunction.

The black-market economy surrounding the sale of Tartarian artifacts, especially those tied to Aetheric Power. A high-stakes trade dominated by factions like the Reclaimers Guild and opposed by the Mud Monarchs and Forgotten Order.

A thriving black market for Tartarian relics. Common relics have minor abilities, while rarer artifacts, such as those containing Aetheric energy, can command enormous prices due to their power and instability.

A feared second cataclysm theorized by some factions. Revising or misusing Aetheric technology, environmental shifts, or cosmic disturbances could trigger another disaster like the original Mud Flood.

An Aetheric artifact that emits an Aetheric energy field within arm's reach. It can give an advantage on up to three creatures once per long rest, but if damaged, it may release a destructive Aetheric blast.

Tartarians who died sealed in their homes during the Great Mud Flood, now uncovered by the True Tartarians as they reclaim underground spaces. Treated with reverence, their bones are reburied on shelves lining thousands of miles of tunnels, serving as solemn reminders of Tartaria's lost legacy.

The general population, unaware of Tartaria's history or the existence of Aetheric technology. Their ignorance is maintained by factions like the Mud Monarchs and Conspiracy Architects for social control.
A small but powerful Tartarian relic that can unlock ancient Tartarian doors and machines.

Semi-conscious Aetheric-powered machines built by the Tartarian Giants to guard their cities. Many still patrol the buried ruins, learning and adapting across centuries; some have developed quirks from prolonged Aetherstone exposure.

The magic system developed by the True Tartarians during their underground exile. Practitioners draw on Aetherstone to shape earth and stone, construct temporary golems, and mend wounds. Heavy use leaves the caster scarred in body or mind.

factions.definition: A covert cabal focused on protecting humanity from the dangers of Aetheric technology by suppressing knowledge of Tartaria. They control global narratives to keep the Unknowing Masses ignorant of Tartaria's existence. Allied with the Mud Monarchs.

A secretive group of Tartarian scholars and engineers seeking to revive Aetheric Power for humanity's benefit. Often opposed by the Mud Monarchs, they conduct covert operations to rediscover Tartaria's lost knowledge.

A global faction of survivors from Tartaria's royal bloodlines who control the few remaining Aetheric technologies. They suppress knowledge of Tartaria, fearing the loss of their influence over modern society.

A network of treasure hunters and scavengers who sell Tartarian relics on the black market. Although not aligned with any faction, they clash with the Mud Monarchs and the Forgotten Order over control of valuable artifacts.

A religious faction that venerates Tartarian Giants, believing in their eventual return to restore Tartaria. They conduct rituals at Tartarian ruins, hoping to awaken the giants and reclaim the lost empire.
A hybrid religious-scientific group that studies Tartarian architecture as a divine and technological achievement, striving to replicate the secrets of Architectural Sorcery for a new era.

A radical faction intent on restoring Tartaria at any cost, even if it means triggering another cataclysm like the Mud Flood. They are dedicated to reactivating Aetheric Power systems and achieving Tartaria's former glory. Led by Sasha Ironheart.

important_people.definition: A Tartarian philosopher-scientist whose pioneering research on Aetheric frequency resonance and experiments with the Aetheric Engine in Thametan's Tower led to the catastrophic Great Mud Flood, which ultimately buried much of Tartaria.

A historian obsessed with uncovering Tartaria's secrets, using any means necessary to further his studies. Known for his willingness to betray allies if it brings him closer to Tartaria's lost knowledge.
Leader of the Tartarian Revivalists, who believes that reviving the Tartarian Giants could be humanity's salvation. Her dedication and fervor make her a formidable and occasionally dangerous figure.
A seasoned mercenary hired to protect Tartarian expeditions. Known for a murky past and unpredictable loyalty, Volkov often sways between factions based on the rewards offered.
A treasure hunter fascinated by Tartarian relics, whose loyalty is often unpredictable and driven by the value of her discoveries.

A reclusive and enigmatic sponsor of expeditions who supplies ancient maps and resources to those willing to seek Tartaria's lost secrets. His true motives remain hidden, making him an ambiguous ally.

important_places.definition: A broken spine of scrub and stacked stone east of the Tartarian Outskirts, cut everywhere with raider sign — spiral-marks, ridge-signs, tallies. The border gangs stage and settle things here, past the reach of the outposts and their truce.

The long broken stair climbing to the Giant Vault's sealed doors. The mud on the landings has trembled since the Titan began to walk, and what its footfalls woke does not sleep inside the Vault — it waits out on the steps.

Drakova's flooded eastern district, outside the sealed core. Streets passable only by pole-raft, roofs at the waterline, and reed-choked shallows where the Mud Siren keeps its roost — the drowned it has taken still work the water for it.

The ancient capital city of Tartaria, home to the Grand Spire of Asgardar, a towering structure on the city's outskirts that once channeled Aetheric Power from cosmic sources into the city's energy grid.

The southernmost wound in the world, lying directly beneath the Mud Flood Nexus — a chasm system that simply keeps going down. Unlike every other way into the Aetherstone Deep it is neither vault nor seal nor guarded chamber; it is a floor that ends. Heat and a faint grid-hum come up out of it, and the Grand Spire of Etheria stands on its floor two miles west of the descent.

The collector-tower of the drowned capital, standing alone on the outskirts where Asgardar's last ring of streets gives out. Fourteen tiers of it remain above the silt. Not to be confused with the Grand Spire of Etheria, a separate and taller tower now lying at the bottom of the Black Reach.

A monumental tower standing on the floor of the Black Reach, two miles west of the descent, known for drawing Aetheric energy from the celestial realms; considered one of Tartaria's most powerful Aetheric structures. The chasm took it whole and it is still standing.
A prominent Tartarian city and an experimental hub where Thametan's Tower was built to advance research on Aether.

An experimental tower in Samarran containing the Aetheric Engine, a device created to push the boundaries of Aetheric Power. Its malfunction led to the Great Mud Flood, a disaster that buried Tartaria in Aetherstone mud.
A significant Tartarian city deeply affected by the Great Mud Flood, rumored to contain hidden remnants of Tartaria's ancient Aetheric technology.
A partially buried city in Tartaria, home to the Red Tower, rumored to house one of the last operational Aetheric Cores.
A mysterious structure in Nimari, believed to contain a functional Aetheric Core, making it a critical location for factions seeking to revive Tartarian technology.
A hidden base of the Forgotten Order, located on the edge of the Great Tartary Plains. It is a stronghold for those dedicated to recovering Tartaria's lost Aetheric knowledge.
A vast, Aetheric-charged expanse covering ancient Tartaria, known for unpredictable phenomena like magnetic anomalies, Aetheric storms, and temporal distortions.
A legendary Lost Capital of Tartaria, hidden beneath layers of Aetherstone mud and believed to hold a powerful Aetheric Core, drawing explorers and factions alike.

A formation of black, magnetically charged spires that rise from the mud near a former Tartarian observatory. The pillars disrupt technology, and their location suggests they may have once been part of a cosmic energy center.

A vast staircase descending into the mud, its endpoint completely submerged. Believed to lead to one of Tartaria's greatest cities, but Aetheric disturbances prevent explorers from reaching its depths.

A group of sharp, towering spires jutting from shallow waters, attracting explorers with their architectural mysteries. The area is home to dangerous mud sirens which protect the ruins from intruders.
The partially submerged steeple of a grand Tartarian cathedral. Said to contain a powerful Tartarian artifact, but no explorers who have entered have returned.

A pocket within the Mud Seas where the sky glows with residual Aetheric energy. The area is filled with wrecked ships and frozen statues of former crew members, an eerie reminder of the power of Aetheric storms.

Treacherous shallow, murky waters covering Tartarian ruins, formed after the Great Mud Flood. Aetheric energy within the mud creates disorienting magnetic distortions and dangerous storms, making navigation treacherous.

An ancient Tartarian vault believed to hold the last resting place of the Tartarian Giants. Legends claim it contains relics of immense power, but it is unclear if the giants within are protectors or a dormant threat.

The subterranean control center believed to have regulated the disastrous Great Mud Flood. Restoring or deactivating this site's systems could influence the stability of Aetheric energy, making it a focal point for factional conflicts.

The primary power source and control hub for Tartarian technology. Hidden deep within Tartarian ruins, the Aetheric Chamber contains machinery to control Aetheric energy, heavily guarded by ancient automatons and Aetheric traps.

The regions surrounding Tartarian cities, littered with defenses, dormant traps, and relics of Aetheric technology. Explorers often find clues about Tartaria's inner workings here, but must navigate Aetheric anomalies and ancient defense systems.

Formerly vibrant Tartarian cities now sealed beneath Aetherstone mud. These cities hold Tartaria's most powerful secrets, preserved by impenetrable mud that resists excavation, where Aetheric energy creates time distortions and magnetic anomalies.

The northeastern mountain capital, frost-wreathed where every other Lost Capital drowned warm — the gate-city to the Giants' tombs. The Servants of the Giants kept the long vigil here before the Flood, and its Core sleeps under a cold-stone in the deep keep.

The Eternal Dynasty's river capital in the far-eastern wetlands, half-submerged in slow current. Its Core seat is ringed by a still pool the Riverbinder bound to the housing with a cantor's chord; the water has not moved since the Flood.

The Conspiracy Architects' hidden capital in the far northwest — a maze of false doors and overlaid corridors where every map is wrong by design. The true Core seat is said to stand behind the door you didn't see.

The Forgotten Order's ritual seat in the southern band — halls of binding-sigils carved into black basalt. Its Core is kept under a chain of seals only a Sealwarden can read, which is why the Order guards its reading jealously.

A deep, self-sufficient True Tartarian enclave hollowed beneath the Buried Cities — Aethercraft-shaped mud walls and ancestor-shrines to the fallen Giants. Its Seekers walk the labyrinthine tunnels for relics, and outsiders find it only when the Enclave decides to be found.

A weathered ring of standing stones on the contested eastern flats where rival factions meet under truce. No faction holds it; the banners change with the season, and the stones have outlasted every agreement sworn between them.

The Mud Monarchs' frontier toll-court — the last ordered ground before the buried capitals. A seneschal logs every traveler who passes toward the deeper cities, and the ledgers go back further than the Monarchs like to admit.

An old garrison of the Eternal Dynasty kept lit at the edge of the ruins. The oath-stones are still standing, and the road past them runs down into the flooded capitals — every Dynasty soldier walks it once, going, and once more if they are lucky.

A rest-camp of True Tartarian pilgrims on the frontier track, where the faithful gather before the long descent into the deep buried cities. The fires are kept low and the songs lower; the road they rest for does not forgive noise.

A Stone Builders' staging post at the safe edge of the ruin-field — theodolite stakes, chalked plans, stacked shoring timber. The Builders measure twice here because past this camp the ground stops honoring measurements.

A roadside vigil-shrine of the Servants of the Giants on the frontier, where keepers wait and watch before the long road down to the giant vaults. The watch has not been broken since the Flood; the keepers do not say what they are watching for.

A Tartarian Revivalist dig-and-press camp at the lip of the wastes — crates of equipment, a printing trestle, and a map-board marking the capitals they mean to make headlines of. The truth gets dug up here, and typeset shortly after.

A Reclaimers' Guild salvage-stake driven into the frontier mud on the western edge — claim-posts, a tally-board of marked ruins, and a winch rig for hauling up whatever the wastes give. Every Guild expedition into the deep country launches from here.

A Conspiracy of Architects observation-blind disguised as a collapsed waystation on the western frontier. Behind the false rubble: a map-wall of routes the public must never connect, and a quiet door onto the road.

A neutral-ground bazaar that does not advertise itself — four canvas stalls in a wind-scoured hollow of the Sunken Middens. Agents of every faction trade under an unspoken truce; the market keeps no ledger, asks no questions, and moves if it is ever written down on a map.

timeline_events.name: The Lost Covenant of the Giants
timeline_events.summary: Tartarian Giants refuse to share Aetheric secrets and retreat to the Ural Mountains. The schism weakens the empire's leadership.

timeline_events.name: The Aetheric Conflux War
timeline_events.summary: A critical Conflux malfunctions near the Caspian Sea. Rebels and rogue nobles try to seize the surge. Whole regions are cut off from the Aetheric grid — the first visible cracks in Tartarian dominance.

timeline_events.name: Fall of the Tartarian Capital
timeline_events.summary: Thametan's Aetheric Engine pushes Aetheric resonance past its envelope. Mud charged with Aether rises through the empire and entombs it. Surviving nobles flee to the highest spires and become the Mud Monarchs.

timeline_events.name: The Aetheric Accords
timeline_events.summary: Tartarian noble families sign accords in the Urals to safeguard surviving Aetheric technology. The Mud Monarchs consolidate from this treaty.

timeline_events.name: The Reclaimers' Uprising
timeline_events.summary: Beneath Paris, Reclaimers strike a violent compromise with the Forgotten Order and Mud Monarchs. The Reclaimers Guild is formalized as the black market in Tartarian relics.

timeline_events.name: The Northern Plague (Aetheric Rot)
timeline_events.summary: A plague linked to malfunctioning relics breaks out in Siberia. The Mud Monarchs attempt containment; entire underground cities are abandoned and lost.

timeline_events.name: The Munich Coup
timeline_events.summary: The Conspiracy Architects split from the Mud Monarchs, seizing relics and tightening control over what the world is allowed to remember about Tartaria.

timeline_events.name: The Great Purge of Forgotten Knowledge
timeline_events.summary: Conspiracy Architects and allied governments destroy Tartarian archives beneath Istanbul. The historical record of the empire is wiped to near-myth.

timeline_events.name: The Antarctic Aetheric Pulse
timeline_events.summary: An Aetheric pulse beneath the Antarctic ice draws a Forgotten Order expedition. Sabotage and discovery both follow; the existence of a global Aetheric network beneath Tartaria's outposts is hinted at.

timeline_events.name: The Singapore Relic Seizure
timeline_events.summary: Reclaimers outmaneuver both the Mud Monarchs and the Forgotten Order to capture a major Tartarian relic cache. Relic-hunting interest spikes across Southeast Asia.
